newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin aide to address Davos forum on NATO--TASS.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin aide to address Davos forum on NATO--TASS.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's most senior aide will address the World Economic Forum in Davos to outline Russia's position on NATO's plans to expand eastwards, Itar-Tass news agency said on Saturday.

It quoted "well informed Kremlin soruces" as saying that Yeltsin's chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais is expected to speak on Monday at the meeting of international political and business leaders held in the Swiss mountain resort.
Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday that the Kremlin leader, who is convalescing after pneumonia in his country residence, had approved a speech written personally by Chubais.

Moscow strongly opposes the Western alliance's expansion plans. But after NATO made clear that Russia's objections could not stop the expansion, Moscow has moved to work out a deal with the alliance to guarantee its national security interests.
Tass quoted the Kremlin source as saying that the Chubais speach will be "pretty tough" but refused to give any further details.
Officials were not immediately availabe for comments.
Yeltsin is expected to discuss NATO expansion with French President Jaques Chirac who will briefly visit Moscow on Sunday.
